subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which Hindu festival is celebrated by throwing coloured powders and water?
questions.explain: Holi is the festival of colours, celebrating spring and the victory of good over evil.

questions.q: Which path to moksha emphasises selfless action and duty without attachment to results?
questions.explain: Karma yoga is the path to moksha through selfless action and performing one's duty without attachment.

questions.q: Which deity in the Trimurti is known as the preserver?
questions.explain: Vishnu is the preserver in the Trimurti, protecting and sustaining the universe.

questions.q: What do many Hindus believe about the relationship between the atman and Brahman?
options: That the soul is destroyed at death
That atman is part of, and ultimately one with, Brahman
That there are many separate eternal souls and no Brahman
questions.explain: Many Hindus believe the atman (inner self) is part of, and ultimately one with, Brahman.

questions.q: What is the term for Hindu worship, often performed at a home shrine or mandir?
questions.explain: Puja is the act of worship in Hinduism, often involving offerings and prayer.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four aims of life (Purusharthas)?
questions.explain: Moksha (liberation) is one of the four aims of life, with dharma, artha and kama.

questions.q: What is 'samsara' in Hinduism?
options: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
questions.explain: Samsara is the continuous cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

questions.q: What is a Hindu temple called?
questions.explain: A mandir is a Hindu temple, a place of worship that houses murtis of the deities.

questions.q: The four ashramas describe the four:
questions.explain: The ashramas are the four stages of life: student, householder, retirement and renunciation.

questions.q: What is the law of karma?
options: The duty of a particular caste
The principle that actions have consequences
questions.explain: Karma is the principle that a person's actions affect their future and future lives.

questions.q: The Hindu festival of Diwali is best known as the festival of:
questions.explain: Diwali is the festival of lights, celebrating the triumph of good over evil and light over darkness.

questions.q: Diwali in many traditions recalls the return of which figure after defeating the demon Ravana?
questions.explain: Diwali often celebrates the return of Rama to Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana.

questions.q: What does 'dharma' refer to in Hinduism?
questions.explain: Dharma refers to duty, righteousness and the proper way of living.

questions.q: In Hinduism, what is the name for the ultimate, supreme reality or spirit?
questions.explain: Brahman is the ultimate reality or supreme spirit underlying all existence in Hinduism.

questions.q: Which three deities make up the Hindu Trimurti?
questions.explain: The Trimurti is Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver and Shiva the destroyer.

questions.q: Bhakti yoga is the path to moksha based mainly on:
questions.explain: Bhakti yoga seeks moksha through loving devotion and worship of a personal deity.

questions.q: Which of the four aims of life (Purusharthas) refers to lawful wealth and prosperity?
questions.explain: Artha is the aim of seeking lawful wealth and material wellbeing in life.

questions.q: Rama and Krishna are usually understood in Hinduism as:
questions.explain: Rama and Krishna are widely regarded as avatars, earthly incarnations of the god Vishnu.

questions.q: Jnana yoga is the path to moksha through:
questions.explain: Jnana yoga is the path of knowledge and wisdom, realising the unity of atman with Brahman.

questions.q: What is a 'murti' in Hindu worship?
options: A sacred image or statue of a deity
questions.explain: A murti is a sacred image or statue of a deity used as a focus for worship in puja.

questions.q: Which scripture is a famous dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna?
questions.explain: The Bhagavad Gita records Krishna's teachings to the warrior Arjuna.

questions.q: What is 'moksha' in Hindu belief?
options: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
The law of cause and effect
questions.explain: Moksha is release or liberation from samsara, the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.
